data.name: Artadokht
data.gender_notes: Artadokht is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Daughter of the god Artaxerxes, goddess of wisdom and divine protection. The name Artadokht carries the meaning “Divine gift, goddess of wisdom” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Persian. Parents who choose Artadokht usually hope their child will grow to embody divine gift, goddess of wisdom and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the protection and blessings of Allah, the divine gift bestowed upon a child
data.etymology: Artadokht belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Divine gift, goddess of wisdom.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Artadokht total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.
data.cultural_impact: The name "Artadokht" carries Persian origins, derived from the name of the ancient Iranian god Artaxerxes, who was associated with royal power, fortune, and wisdom. The name "Artadokht" is significant in Persian and Islamic culture as it symbolizes the powerful connection between godly influence and human wisdom.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, the name "Artadokht" holds spiritual significance as a reminder of the divine protection and provisions that come from Allah. The name "Artadokht" invokes the spirit of reverence and submission to the will of God, emphasizing the importance of seeking wisdom and knowledge from the Quran and Hadiths. By carrying this name, individuals are encouraged to strive for spiritual growth and inner wisdom, ultimately bringing them closer to Allah.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Divine gift, goddess of wisdom" symbolizes Daughter of the god Artaxerxes, goddess of wisdom and divine protection. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Artadokht serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of divine gift, goddess of wisdom.

historical_references.reference: Artadokht was a Persian princess of the Sassanid Empire, daughter of King Khosrow I Anushirvan and sister of Hormizd IV.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Artadokht remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.

name_in_real_life.story: Fatima Artadokht, a teacher in Karachi, Pakistan, shares that their name Artadokht meaning "Divine gift, goddess of wisdom" has been a source of inspiration throughout their life, motivating them to be a positive influence in their community.
